<!-- pr-reviewer: ee7270eed4e0ea1fa7e7f115f55c1a10b8869514 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** One test that is green on `main` is red on the trial merge.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code (new G2/G3 output for the wire posts), the wire gouge laws and the wire verifier in `camcraft-sim`.

## What looks good

- The analytic offset (`arc_offset.rs`) refuses each failure case by name: an inside arc tighter than the kerf, a consumed parallel, a neck, and parallels that do not meet. Nothing is clamped.
- Two independent checks guard the output. The motion kerf law reads the drawing exactly (`arc_laws.rs`). The sim verifier reads each arc as chords and subtracts the chord sagitta (`kerf.rs`, `arcs.rs`).
- A tabbed cut with arcs and an arc on a leaning wire are "unreadable" by name. They never pass silently.
- The exact-polygon path of #3180 stays byte for byte (`exact_polygon()`).
- I read the six new goldens against the drawings, line by line:
  - `wire_dxf_die_circle.nc` (ISO, G-EDM, Sodick): lead X6 Y5 to X10.835 Y5, then two G3 half turns of radius 4.835 about X6 Y5, then the lead-out. 4.835 = 5 - 0.165. This is correct.
  - `wire_dxf_punch_fillet.nc`: the drawing walks counter-clockwise (the shoelace sum of its corners is positive). Each of the four outside corners has a G3 pivot of radius 0.165 about the corner. The inside corner at X6 Y5 is trimmed to X5.835 Y5.165. The fillet is `G3 X13. Y15.165 I-3.165 J0.`: centre X13 Y12, radius 3 + 0.165. The lead from X6 Y25 stays outside the punch. This is correct.
- The new modules have provenance lines. The new files are under 400 lines. Clippy is clean.

## Results, merged with main (locally, macOS)

Trial merge: PR head `ee7270eed` + upstream/main `02d05bc1c`. The merge is clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `motion build`, `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: wire_fans` | ok |
| `sim suites: lib` | ok |
| `post build` + 49 `post suites` (all `script_*` posts, `recorded_streams`, `agie_inspection`) | ok |
| `app build (--no-run)`, `app suites: lib` | ok |
| `cl suites: headless_bin` | ok |
| `app suites`: all 17 `wire_*` suites, `wire_dxf_selection`, `g_edm_post`, 4 `sodick_*`, `edm_*`, `verify`, `verify_arc_reading`, `golden_cl`, `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`, `project_roundtrip`, `commands_undo`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `mcp_dxf`, `feature_pick_wire`, 4 `contour_dxf_*`, `slot_dxf_sketch`, `sketch_profile` | ok |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | ok |
| **`app suites: agie_native`** | **FAIL** (35 passed, 1 failed) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The failing test, on the trial merge (it fails again when run alone):

```
---- tangent::a_short_inner_offgrid_edge_or_folded_loop_publishes_nothing stdout ----
panicked at crates/app/tests/agie_native/tangent.rs:99:9:
convex loop: ... generation refused: invalid machining parameters: wire contour: the start hole at X0.000 Y-21.000 lies inside the profile - a punch is cut from outside it; the wire would burn through the punch
```

The same test on bare upstream/main `02d05bc1c` (same worktree, same build): **ok**. Main did not change any wire, Agie or post code after the PR base `b13ebd440`. Thus this PR causes the failure.

Not run: the quick plan also names about 600 other `app` suites. The plan names them only because they share `tests/golden/nc/` as test input, or the `app::operation` gate map. I did not run them, because the verdict is already "needs changes". The light lane did not run.

**Extra suites run** (user selection): no file under `testdata/` changed, and no importer code changed. Thus no extra suites apply.

## Mutations (safety tier)

1. Pivot arc radius `k` changed to `0.9 * k` in `arc_offset.rs`:
   - `motion suites: lib` is red: `line_and_arc_die_trims_outside_corners_and_pivots_the_reentrant_one`, `line_and_arc_punch_pivots_outside_corners_and_trims_the_inside_corner`;
   - `wire_dxf_selection` is red: `arcs::line_and_arc_punch_pivots_its_corners_and_posts_its_goldens`.
2. The kerf offset moved 2 um into the product (`k - 0.002` in `arc_cut.rs`), and the motion kerf law disabled (`arc_laws::kerf` returns `Ok` at once). Thus only the sim verifier can see the gouge. `wire_dxf_selection` is red at `arcs.rs:63`: the verifier gives `Gouge { depth: 0.002 }` for the die circle and for the punch.

Both mutations are reverted. The tree is clean.

## Requested before merge

1. **`crates/app/tests/agie_native/tangent.rs:90-94` is red because of this PR.** The PR body says that `agie_native` is ok, but on this head it fails.
   - Cause: `run_job_arms` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:211-217`) now sends each selected chain that is not an exact polygon to `generate_arcs` first, also for the Agie machine. Before, `nominal_ring` sent a punch to `WireProfile`, which refused a loop that is not convex and tangent ("convex loop").
   - The case with the arc from 180 to 360 degrees makes a lower half circle down to Y-29. This shape encloses the start hole X0 Y-21. Thus the new refusal "lies inside the profile" is geometrically correct. The program is still refused, and nothing is published. The defect is the stale test, not unsafe output.
   - Fix: update the test to the new route and keep its intent. For example, move the start hole of that case out of the half circle, so that the native door still gives "convex loop". Or assert the new refusal text for that case. Then record the change of refusal order for the Agie machine in `docs/decisions/3937-wire-dxf-arcs.md`.
   - Class: the PR changes which door refuses first for a selected Agie chain. Please run the whole `agie_native` suite (`cargo xtask gate quick --only "app suites: agie_native"`) and each other suite that asserts a refusal text of a selected-chain door. Then name the result in the PR body.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was 4,606 lines and is now 4,617 lines. It was already over the 400-line limit. This PR does not cause that.
- The verifier gives the gouge of mutation 2 at `move_no: 1` (the lead-in end), not at an arc move. This is correct, because the lead ends on the path. But a move number on the arc would help the user more. This is a possible follow-up (P7).
- Heavy step: the PR body says that no `#[ignore]` heavy test covers `motion::wire_edm` or `sim::verify::wire`. I agree, from the dry run. Thus no targeted heavy step applies.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

This PR is a draft again. The quick gate result in the body was wrong: the log that I read came from an earlier run on a different branch. The real quick gate on `ee7270eed` did not complete. I now run the quick gate again on this head. I will update the body with the real result, and then flag the PR ready again.

Reply to the review of `ee7270eed` (pr-reviewer, 23:38Z).

**Finding 1 (`agie_native/tangent.rs` red): fixed in `6b503900f`.** This commit closes that finding. The new head waits for a fresh review.

- I accept the cause. The arc door now refuses first for a selected Agie chain that is not an exact polygon.
- The half circle 180-360 with the hole X0 Y-21 now asserts "lies inside the profile". This pins the new order.
- I added one case with the hole at X-19 Y-24, outside the half circle. The native door does not refuse this case. The arc door refuses the sharp inside corner at X14 Y-14 first ("an inside corner or slot of the profile near X14.000 Y-14.000"). Thus this drawing cannot reach the native door.
- The half circle 0-180 still pins the native "convex loop" refusal. The native refusal thus stays tested.
- `docs/decisions/3937-wire-dxf-arcs.md` records the refusal order, and the PR body says it too.

**Results on `6b503900f` (Mac):**

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 762 steps, 762 ok, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The plan holds `agie_native` (36 ok), `wire_dxf_selection`, `g_edm_post`, the four `sodick_*` suites, each `wire_*` suite, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `script_agie_native` and `script_sodick_wire`. All are ok.
- Suites that assert a refusal text of a selected-chain door: `agie_native`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_contour`, `wire_post`, `wire_verify`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_4axis`, `sodick_wire_passes`, `sodick_wire_post`, `golden_cl`, `tool_dxf_profile`, `script_agie_native`. All are ok in the plan. Post `agie_safe_setup` is not in the plan. I ran it by name: 22 ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The light lane (6/6 ok) and the wider strict clippy ran on `ee7270eed`. The fix changes only one test and the decision file.

**Draft state.** The PR went to draft because the earlier Gate text in the body was false. That text came from a log of a different branch. I withdrew it, and the body now gives the real gate above. The PR is ready again with a real gate.

Note (not blocking): I did not change the move number of the verifier. It stays a possible P7 follow-up.

New head: `6b503900f`. Ready for a re-check.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a re-review of the new head `6b503900f`. The one earlier finding is fixed. I found no new blocker.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes posted G-code (new G2/G3 output for the wire posts), the wire gouge laws and the wire verifier in `camcraft-sim`.

## Earlier findings (review of `ee7270eed`)

1. **`crates/app/tests/agie_native/tangent.rs` was red.** Fixed in `6b503900f`.
   - The lower half circle (180-360) with the hole X0 Y-21 now asserts "lies inside the profile". This pins the new refusal order.
   - A new case moves the hole to X-19 Y-24, outside the half circle. It asserts the inside-corner refusal near X14.000 Y-14.000.
   - The upper half circle (0-180) still asserts the native "convex loop" refusal. Thus the native door stays tested.
   - `docs/decisions/3937-wire-dxf-arcs.md` records the refusal order and the dropped option (a bypass of the arc door for the Agie machine). The PR body says it too.
   - `app suites: agie_native` is ok on the trial merge (below).

The fix commit changes only that test and the decision file. No production code and no golden changed since the earlier review. Thus the earlier line-by-line reading of the six new goldens stays valid.

## Results, merged with main (locally, macOS)

Trial merge: PR head `6b503900f` + upstream/main `f2a2b8dee`. The merge is clean. Main changed after the earlier review (tool catalog, `mcp` tests, guide pages). No wire, Agie or post code changed on main.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `motion build`, `motion suites: lib`, `motion suites: wire_fans` | ok |
| `sim suites: lib` | ok |
| `post build` + 49 `post suites` (all `script_*` posts, `recorded_streams`, `agie_inspection`, `post_engine`) | ok |
| `cl suites: headless_bin` | ok |
| `app build (--no-run)`, `app suites: lib` | ok |
| `app suites: agie_native` | ok |
| `app suites`: `wire_dxf_selection`, `g_edm_post`, 4 `sodick_*`, 17 other `wire_*` suites, `edm_conditions`, `edm_machine`, `verify`, `verify_arc_reading`, `golden_cl`, `recorded_post_streams`, `posting`, `project_roundtrip`, `commands_undo`, `conformance` | ok (35 steps) |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | ok |
| `app suites`: `mcp`, `mcp_wire_contour`, `mcp_dxf`, `mcp_generate`, `mcp_verify`, `feature_pick_wire`, 4 `contour_dxf_*`, `slot_dxf_sketch`, `sketch_profile`, `tool_dxf_profile`, `tool_dxf_profile_mcp`, `tool_catalog_fields`, `circular_arcs`, `short_arc_lattice`, `first_part_programs`, `operations`, `cli`, `waterjet_profile`, `plasma_profile`, `sinker_cavity_outline` | ok |
| `ui build (--no-run)` + the 6 `ui suites` of the quick plan | ok |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test agie_safe_setup` | ok (22 passed) |
| `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` | ok (6 steps, 0 failed) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: about 600 other `app suites` of the quick plan. The plan names them only because they share `tests/golden/nc/` as test input, or the `app::operation` gate map. The author ran the full quick plan on this head (762 steps, 762 ok, against base `b13ebd4`). Main changed no code that those suites read for this diff.

Heavy step: `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` reaches the `app` and `motion` heavy lanes through the crate edges. No file in `motion::wire_edm`, `sim::verify::wire`, `wire_dxf_selection` or `agie_native` has an `#[ignore]` test. Thus no targeted heavy step covers the changed code (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review"). I agree with the PR body.

**Extra suites run** (user selection): no file under `testdata/` changed, and no importer code changed. Thus no extra suites apply. The six new `.nc` files are the only recorded programs in the diff. Each one is listed under "Goldens moved".

## Mutations (safety tier, run again on this head)

1. Pivot arc radius `k` changed to `0.9 * k` (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/arc_offset.rs:101`):
   - `motion suites: lib` is red: `line_and_arc_die_trims_outside_corners_and_pivots_the_reentrant_one`, `line_and_arc_punch_pivots_outside_corners_and_trims_the_inside_corner`.
   - `app suites: wire_dxf_selection` is red: `arcs::line_and_arc_punch_pivots_its_corners_and_posts_its_goldens`.
2. Offset moved 2 um into the product (`sign * (k - 0.002)` at `arc_cut.rs:77`), and the motion kerf law ignored (`arc_cut.rs:127`). Thus only the sim verifier can see the gouge.
   - `app suites: wire_dxf_selection` is red at `arcs.rs:63`. The verifier gives `Gouge { depth: 0.0020 }` for the die circle and for the punch.

Both mutations are reverted. The tree is clean.

## Law check

- Prime Directive: the new production code has no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!()`. Each failure case of the offset gives a named refusal. Nothing is clamped.
- No UI change. No change to `build.rs`, `.github/`, `scripts/`, `Cargo.toml`, `xtask/` or a process file.
- No snapshot PNG changed.
- The body has `Fixes #3937`, a `Changelog:` line, the readings, the pinning tests and "Goldens moved".

## Optional, non-blocking

- `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` was already over the 400-line limit before this PR. The PR adds 11 lines.
- The verifier reports the gouge of mutation 2 at `move_no: 1` (the lead-in end). A move number on the arc would help the user more. A possible `P7` follow-up.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 6b503900fe1dcfef92b2180811ab9587338b1404 -->
**Verdict: Needs changes before merge.** Newer main causes one new compile blocker at two test literals.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The PR changes wire G-code, kerf checks, and the simulation verifier.

## Earlier findings

1. The stale refusal test in `agie_native/tangent.rs` is **fixed** in `6b503900f`. The lower semicircle now asserts the start-hole refusal. The added outside-hole case asserts the inside-corner refusal. The upper semicircle still tests the native refusal. The decision file records this order. I ran the whole `agie_native` suite: 37 passed.

The clean review posted during this run used main `f2a2b8dee`. This review uses newer main `b556d4acd96fa1789ca5cf9c2dfce872624c97df`. The blocker below comes from that newer main. It was not present on the earlier review's base.

## NEW blocker

1. **`crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs:49` and `:135`: the arc suite does not compile with current main.** Main commit `c07eee4d1` moved the wire start position into `WireContourOp.picks`. Both new literals still set the removed `start` field.

   The quick gate, the light build, and strict clippy give:

   ```text
   error[E0560]: struct `camcraft_app::operation::WireContourOp` has no field named `start`
     --> crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs:49:9
   error[E0560]: struct `camcraft_app::operation::WireContourOp` has no field named `start`
      --> crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs:135:35
   ```

   I ran `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wire_dxf_selection --no-run` on bare upstream/main `b556d4acd`: it passes. Thus this is a new integration failure, not a pre-existing main failure.

   Update both literals to `PathPicks` with a `PathPick::xy` start point. The updated `wire_op()` in the parent test module shows the current form. Then run `wire_dxf_selection`, the quick gate, the light lane, and strict clippy again. Update the PR body with those results.

## Local validation

Trial merge `608b119bee5aa8961f9f4ddfa2ac4aa6e2d4622b` merges cleanly. Its first parent is the full PR head named above. No GitHub runner was used.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | FAIL at app build: the two E0560 errors above. The first 55 steps pass. Later steps do not run. |
| CL `headless_bin` | 3 passed |
| Post build and 49 selected post suites | All pass; post lib has 150 passed |
| Sim lib | 252 passed |
| Motion build, lib, `wire_fans` | Pass; motion lib has 640 passed, 22 ignored |
| App `agie_native` | 37 passed |
| App `example_catalog` | 41 passed, 4 ignored |
| App `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | 1 passed each |
| App `golden_cl` | 34 passed |
| App `sodick_wire_passes`, `sodick_wire_post`, `tool_dxf_profile` | 5, 8, 6 passed |
| App `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_post` | 8, 3, 8, 12 passed |
| App `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_verify` | 10, 5, 3 passed |
| Post `agie_safe_setup` | 22 passed |
| `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main` | 5 steps pass; release build fails with the same two E0560 errors |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | FAIL with the same two E0560 errors |

**Extra suites run:** The changed fixture directory is `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/`. I searched its readers. The full quick plan selects the app suites for this shared input. The build failure prevents that full set from running. The named golden and refusal suites above ran separately. `wire_dxf_selection`, which reads all six new goldens, cannot compile. No `testdata/` or importer code changes; no extra kernel import suite applies.

## Safety checks

I read all six new NC goldens line by line. All six are listed under "Goldens moved". No other recorded program changes.

- Die circle: lead X6 Y5 to X10.835 Y5; two G3 half turns about X6 Y5; radius 4.835 = 5 - 0.165; lead-out to the hole.
- Punch: four G3 corner pivots of radius 0.165. The inside corner trims to X5.835 Y5.165. The fillet uses centre X13 Y12 and radius 3.165. ISO, Sodick, and G-EDM agree on the path.

I ran two temporary mutations locally:

1. Pivot radius `k` to `0.9 * k` in `arc_offset.rs`: motion `wire_edm::arc_tests` turns red, with 2 failed. The kerf law reports 0.1485 mm clearance against the required 0.1650 mm.
2. Generation offset `k` to `k - 0.002` in `arc_cut.rs`: the same tests turn red, with 7 failed. This run keeps the kerf law enabled. The app-level isolated-verifier mutation cannot run because the app arc suite does not compile.

Both mutations are reverted. The unchanged arc tests return to green: 11 passed. The worktree is clean.

No ignored heavy test covers the changed wire modules or `wire_dxf_selection`. No full heavy lane ran. No UI, dependency, script, workflow, or process file changes are in the PR diff.

I leave `.claude/worktrees/review-3942` and branch `review-3942` in place to keep the build warm. No code, evidence, or screenshot was committed or pushed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
